public_rationale: The condition has not been established under the contextual reading of a broad AI investment collapse. Reports of a Chinese AI stock crash matter, but they do not establish a collapse of the infrastructure boom described here. No qualifying post-collapse outcome settles the forecast early. Under the conditional-forecast rule, the claim cannot yet be scored. Present-day GPU usefulness does not answer this separate prediction.
limitations: Condition status is unknown, not a finding that no relevant collapse occurred.
The accessible collapse report is secondary reporting of Reuters.
A different interpretation of the collapse's geographic scope could change condition status.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: When the AI bubble bursts, AI infrastructure will not be particularly useful.

statement.excerpt: When the AI bubble bursts, none of this infrastructure will be particularly useful.

our_interpretation: The surrounding passage identifies infrastructure as AI GPUs and data centers built during the investment boom.

The contextual antecedent is a broad collapse of the AI investment boom associated with the named hyperscalers and model companies. A decline in one national stock market does not automatically establish that event.
Useful means substantial productive operation or reuse, whether by original owners or subsequent purchasers. A low resale price alone does not establish uselessness.
No deadline, numerical collapse threshold, or post-collapse observation period is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: After the antecedent is established, broad evidence across the relevant GPUs and data centers shows little substantial productive use or viable reuse.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the antecedent is established, reliable records demonstrate substantial sustained productive use of a material part of the infrastructure. Continued use before a collapse does not settle the forecast.

evidence.excerpt: Other firms have seen similarly sizable drops.
evidence.explanation: The article reports Reuters' account of a sharp Chinese AI and semiconductor stock decline. This is material evidence for a narrower interpretation of bubble burst, but it does not establish a broad collapse of the infrastructure boom described in the post or subsequent infrastructure uselessness.

The article discusses a possible soft landing and investors reassessing AI businesses. It does not establish that the broad antecedent has occurred, and its expectations about future usefulness are not outcome evidence.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Establish a dated collapse of the relevant AI investment boom, then obtain records showing whether its GPUs and data centers retain substantial productive use or largely remain unusable.
